# 16. Works Cited {#references}

[01] [Sphere Association. The Sphere Handbook: Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards in Humanitarian Response, fourth edition, 2018. Behind the Shelter and Food and water factors.](<https://spherestandards.org/handbook/>)

{#reference-01}

[02] United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. Handbook for Emergencies, third edition, 2007. An earlier version of the tool's documentation cited this as the origin of the forty per cent minimum readiness threshold. That attribution has been withdrawn. The handbook is retained here for informing which readiness factors are worth modelling.

{#reference-02}

[03] Inter-Agency Standing Committee. Guidance on humanitarian operations requiring the consent of the host government, 2007. Behind the Authority consent gatekeeper.

{#reference-03}

[04] [Protocol Additional to the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949, and relating to the Protection of Victims of International Armed Conflicts (Protocol I), 1977, Articles 12 and 58. Behind the Medical capacity and Security factors.](<https://ihl-databases.icrc.org/en/ihl-treaties/api-1977>)

{#reference-04}

[05] International Committee of the Red Cross. Publication on violence and the use of force, 2013. Cited as grounding the Security gatekeeper.

{#reference-05}

[06] Park, S.K. and Miller, K.W. (1988). Random Number Generators: Good Ones Are Hard To Find. Communications of the ACM, volume 31, issue 10. The generator used for all seeded randomness in the tool.

{#reference-06}
